title: Passion Fruit Curd Tart in Chocolate Pastry
changes_from_base: A cocoa pastry case and a tangy passion fruit curd lightened with whipped cream, set in the fridge instead of baked.
summary: A twist on the lemon tart: tangy passion fruit curd folded with whipped cream and set in a crisp cocoa pastry case.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: beat the yolk with the 1 tbsp cream. Pulse the flour, cocoa, icing sugar and salt, add the butter and pulse to coarse crumbs, then add the yolk mix and blend until it clumps. Wrap the disc and chill 1 h.

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: roll to a 28 cm round on a floured surface, ease it into the tin, press into the flutes and trim. Freeze 30 min while the oven heats to 190 °C (170 °C fan).

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: line with paper and beans and bake on the tray for 25-30 min, until set and smelling of cocoa. Lift out the beans, bake 5 min more, then cool completely.

steps.title: Juice
steps.text: scoop the passion fruit pulp into the processor and pulse 3-4 times to free the seeds. Push it through the sieve and measure 125 ml juice.

steps.title: Curd
steps.text: whisk the juice, sugar, yolks, lemon juice, cornflour and salt in the saucepan. Stir over medium-low heat for 8-12 min, until thickened and 80 °C on the thermometer. Off the heat whisk in the butter, sieve into a bowl, press cling film on the surface and chill 1 h 30 min. Keep stirring into the corners so no egg catches on the base.

steps.title: Lighten
steps.text: whip the cream to soft peaks. Whisk a third into the cold curd, then fold in the rest until smooth.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: spread the curd in the cooled case and chill at least 8 h, or overnight, until sliceable. A long chill gives clean slices.

tips: Pick wrinkled passion fruit; they are riper and give more juice.
Pulse the pulp only briefly, or broken seeds will speckle the curd.
Cocoa pastry darkens fast, so judge it by smell and a dry surface, not colour.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. The pastry softens slowly after that.
